sample_unit: chatbot platform responses to a single standardized query, rated by 7 neurologists
models_evaluated: 10 widely accessible AI chatbot platforms (specific names not reported in the text)

links.outcome: Readability (FKGL, Coleman-Liau) of chatbot responses relative to recommended public health thresholds
links.effect: All outputs exceeded recommended readability thresholds (FKGL≥8); median FKGL about 17.5 for both paid and free platforms; Coleman-Liau about 21.3 vs 21.7.
links.quote: Readability remained limited: all outputs exceeded recommended public health readability thresholds (FKGL≥8).

links.outcome: Citation transparency of chatbot responses measured with the Web Resource Rating
links.effect: WRR differed significantly across platforms (P<.001). Paid platforms had higher WRR than free ones (median 26.8 vs 10.7; P<.001). Conversation-focused platforms scored higher than search-focused ones (26.8 vs 19.6; P=.001).
links.quote: Paid-access platforms outperformed free-access platforms in DISCERN (median 42, IQR 36-45 vs 33, IQR 23.8-41.3; P<.001), PEMAT-P (median 52.6, IQR 46-54 vs 46, IQR 26.3-47.4; P=.002), and WRR (median 26.8, IQR 23.2-26.8 vs 10.7, IQR 3.57-19.6; P<.001).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates responses from ten AI chatbot platforms to a standardized patient question about a rare neurological disease (MOGAD), rated by neurologists on quality, readability, and citation transparency. It does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
